reason: While this passage (Exodus 1) clearly depicts the Hebrew people suffering greatly under Egyptian oppression—enslaved with hard labor, making bricks and mortar, subjected to harsh taskmasters—the text contains no instance of leaders telling them their suffering is their own fault. The narrative presents Pharaoh's oppression as stemming from his own political fear that the Israelites will multiply and potentially side with his enemies (Exodus 1:9-10). The blame and causation rest entirely with Pharaoh's calculations and decisions, not on any admission of fault by the Israelites themselves or their leaders.
